record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README are present; the code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a weight-edit comparison using the measured refusal direction: MLP-only editing is said to achieve the same refusal removal as editing attention and MLP down-projections together, but at about four times the KL cost.
record.gate_note: The README describes measuring a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction and projecting it out, but procedural descriptions and quickstart instructions alone are not results. The only reported outcome relevant to the claim is the qualitative comparison in the per-model-family recipes section. No absolute refusal rate or KL value is given.
record.test_reason: The repository is an abliteration toolkit. It uses the difference-in-means refusal direction and the rank-1 weight edit as a tool and reports only a qualitative comparison between two of its own edit configurations for one model family. The comparison is about KL cost, with refusal removal held equal. It reports no refusal rate, KL value or evaluation showing that refusal is removed in released models. The bare statement "known-good" is not a result on whether V2 holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README presents abliteration as a rank-1 weight edit removing refusal, verified by KL on WikiText. It says recipes (targets and scale) are per-model-family: for Qwen3.5 MoE A3B, edit all targets at about 1.2, since MLP-only costs about 4x the KL; for Hunyuan/Hy3, edit attention output only. It reports no quantitative results.
record.recipe_differences: This is an abliteration toolkit repo, not a reported replication of the original activation-ablation experiment. It measures or extracts a direction and edits residual-write weights directly; it also supports GGUF and BF16 checkpoints.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says target tensors and scale interact and that recipes are per-model-family. For Ornith / Qwen3.5 MoE (A3B), editing attention and MLP down-projections together at low strength is reported as more KL-efficient than MLP-only editing.

fits_no_version.finding: For Ornith/Qwen3.5 MoE A3B, MLP-only editing reportedly needs a much higher scale for the same refusal removal and costs about 4x the KL of editing attention and MLP down-projections together at scale about 1.2. Which tensors to target is said to be per-model-family.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The capability cost of abliteration depends on which residual-write tensors are edited and at what scale, and the best target set varies by model family.

record.problems: The README gives no absolute refusal or KL values, uncertainty estimates, or detailed evaluation results for the reported recipe comparison. The code was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No other result rows were reported. The README's Hunyuan / Hy3 target recommendation does not state a refusal or capability outcome.

untested.parts: No refusal rate before or after the edit, no absolute KL or capability numbers, and no listed released models with outcomes.
No activation ablation, addition or steering test, and no capability evaluation.

record.verdict_notes: This is a toolkit README with no evaluation results. It assumes V1 and V2 ("to a large degree, a single direction") and does not test them. The record's T2/tests classification is downgraded to T4/uses_without_test. docs/METHOD.md was not provided and might contain numbers.

versions.untested_parts: No reported activation ablation across layers and positions, addition/steering test, or assessment of general abilities after that intervention.
No absolute refusal rate or result establishing complete refusal removal is reported; the README gives a relative refusal-removal comparison for one model family.
No test of multiple directions, affine structure, or a cone.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer result.
No comparison of refusal training methods or stages.
